system_prompt_style.note: Default tool-calling agent: the system prompt is the domain policy wiki, fixed per environment. Alternatives: the ReAct agent concatenates wiki + tool JSON + instruction; the few-shot agent appends randomly sampled examples (templated).

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The agent can only access API tools and domain policies, and indirectly access databases via API tools.
env_context_strategy.note: Closest value. The domain policy is injected up front and the database is explored only through API tools. There is no repository or file tree.

context_compaction.note: The run loop only appends messages. No truncation or summarisation is visible in any of the agents.

observation_format.note: Observations are strings. Some of them may be JSON dumps of database entries.

tool_call_format.note: Default is native function calling (tool-calling strategy). The react and act strategies parse a JSON action from text: chat_react_agent.py:47 "action_str = message.content.split("Action:")[-1].strip()".

tool_count.note: Tools come from the environment. The default README command uses --env retail, which has 16 tool files counted in the file tree (airline also has 16). The paper reports 15 and 13 without think. Registration in __init__ was not seen. The agent itself defines no tools.

edit_primitive.note: The tool registry contains only domain database APIs. There is no file-editing tool.

tool_schema_source.note: Each tool returns its schema dict from get_info(). The concrete tool files were not shown.

protocol_standardization.note: Only a proprietary Tool base class is present. No mcp or a2a files appear in the file tree.

loop_primitives.note: Each step is one model call followed by one action. The ReAct, Act and few-shot strategies are also react loops.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: planning approaches [25] might be too slow to help a user in real time.
planning_granularity.note: The default tool-calling agent has no planning. The react strategy prompts for a one-line Thought, which would be implicit.

multi_agent_topology.note: The LLM user simulator is part of the environment and is not a second agent.

delegation_mechanism.note: No delegation exists. transfer_to_human_agents is a domain tool.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: We use a language model (gpt-4-0613) to simulate a human user interacting with the agent.
human_in_loop.note: The user is simulated and no approval gate exists in the loop. A human-strategy user may exist in envs/user.py, which was not shown.

long_term_memory.note: The loop reads no prior-run data. Few-shot examples are static and are not memory.

state_persistence.note: Every solve starts from a reset. There is no resume path.

self_verification.evidence_quote: self-reflection [19] is unrealistic as real-world agents only have one chance to serve the user
self_verification.note: The reward check is benchmark scoring, not agent self-verification.

retry_policy.note: Multiple trials per task exist for pass^k measurement only.

rollback.note: No undo tool is registered. The environment reset between tasks is a harness reset.

termination_condition.note: The episode also ends on env_response.done, which is triggered by the simulated user's ###STOP### or by the environment. This is not an agent finish tool.

cost_controls.note: Cost is tracked but never capped. model_utils/api/cache.py and router.py exist but were not shown and appear tied to auxiliary tooling.

timeouts.note: No timeout appears in the run loop.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: is deterministic and implemented as a Python function
execution_isolation.note: Tools run in-process on an in-memory database.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: which is hidden from the agent and the user, and can only be read from or written to using API actions
filesystem_access.note: Closest value. The agent has no filesystem access at all, only the JSON database via APIs.

network_policy.evidence_quote: is deterministic and implemented as a Python function
network_policy.note: Closest value. Actions are domain Python functions with no network egress capability. The model API itself is remote.

permission_model.note: Every emitted action is executed. Some policy checks are enforced inside the APIs themselves.

tracing.note: SolveResult carries the full message trajectory. The README describes results files and historical trajectory JSON.

replayability.note: Trajectories are stored for analysis. No replay entry point appears in the file tree.

eval_hooks.note: The repository is itself the benchmark and provides reward and pass^k.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a language agent provided with domain-specific API tools and policy guidelines.
target_domain.note: The domain is customer service (retail and airline).

open_source.note: The licence text was not shown.

primary_artifact.note: The repository was rewritten after the paper (README notice).

first_release_date.note: No tag or first-commit data was in the evidence, so the fallback is the paper v1 date.

pinned_version.evidence_quote: This repository contains outdated versions of the airline and retail tasks.
pinned_version.note: Untagged main commit as given in the evidence header. The full hash was not provided.

stars.evidence_quote: a user (simulated by language models) and a language agent
stars.note: Taken from the evidence header, not from a fresh gh api call.
